title: Families satisfying a local condition form a sheaf of sets
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and $(T_x)_{x\in X}$ a family of sets. Suppose given, for every open $W\subseteq X$, a subset $P(W)\subseteq\prod_{x\in W}T_x$ such that (i) (restriction) for open $W'\subseteq W$ and $f\in P(W)$ the restriction $(f_x)_{x\in W'}$ lies in $P(W')$, and (ii) (locality) a family $f\in\prod_{x\in W}T_x$ lies in $P(W)$ as soon as every $x\in W$ has an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq W$ with $(f_y)_{y\in V}\in P(V)$. Then $W\mapsto P(W)$, with restriction of families as restriction maps, is a sheaf of sets on $X$: for every open covering $W=\bigcup_kW_k$ and families $f^k\in P(W_k)$ that agree on every $W_k\cap W_l$ there is exactly one $f\in P(W)$ restricting to $f^k$ on every $W_k$.
